_skill.name: sub_label_annotation
_skill.description: LLM-facing label catalog (main, sub, segment_type only). Per-label description, hierarchy (parent/children), exclusive_with constraints, and annotation_guideline. Descriptions carry inline VLM / deterministic preflight predicates so hybrid (vector + BM25) similarity over observation text shortlists the matching labels. Circuit and circuit_section labels are NOT in this catalog — the LLM picks them via the `get_circuit_id` / `locate_circuit_section` tools (geometry from app/shared/circuit_sections.py), not by search.
when_to_use: Drilling into a parent-labelled section to pick sub-labels (detailed flow).
Hybrid-similarity shortlist of candidate labels from VLM observations.
Validating label hierarchy (parent presence, mutual exclusion).

range_fit_rule: Whole-range label rule for detailed annotation: every proposed label must describe the proposed child range as a whole. Do not propose a label because it matches only one phase, one apex moment, or a short slice inside the child range; shrink the child range so the label fits throughout, submit a separate proposal for the smaller range, or omit that label.

O.name: Successful Overtake
O.description: Player gained a position on a specific opponent inside the section. Required classifier evidence: `classify_opponent_interaction(start, end)` must return `outcome: pass_completed` with medium/high confidence. Low / weak confidence requires opponent-trajectory inspection or omitting the label. The classifier's primary slot is the opponent to cite. A close opponent with `outcome: failed_attack` is MSR, not O. Defensive holds are OD; failed defenses are MSR.
O.annotation_guideline:
How to identify the sublabels for Successful Overtake: Step 1 — Confirm the pass. Call `classify_opponent_interaction(start, end)`. The result MUST have `outcome: pass_completed` with medium/high confidence. If not, do NOT propose any O sub-label — use the classifier outcome to decide OD, MSR, or no-O. Quote opponent-relative preflight phrases when available, such as opponent started ahead of the driver, driver ended ahead of the opponent, gap flipped from opponent ahead to driver ahead, driver drew alongside the opponent, opponent was on the driver's left/right side, gap to the opponent shrank, driver gained relative speed, driver accelerated better than the opponent, and driver slowed less than the opponent. Step 2 — Pick the technique sub-label from opponent/player position facts, not solo-lap comparisons:
  - O1 (late-brake attack at corner entry): driver drew alongside the opponent under braking and ended ahead.
  - O3 (outside-line sweep through a corner): opponent was on the driver's inside side while the driver stayed outside and ended ahead.
  - O4 (switchback): opponent and driver swapped sides through the corner and the gap flipped from opponent ahead to driver ahead.
  - O5 (slipstream on a straight): gap to the opponent shrank on the straight, driver gained relative speed, and the gap flipped from opponent ahead to driver ahead.

OD.name: Successful Defense
OD.description: Player held position against a real, close opponent inside the section. Required classifier evidence: `classify_opponent_interaction(start, end)` must return `outcome: held_defense` with medium/high confidence. Low / weak confidence requires opponent-trajectory inspection or omitting the label. A merely close opponent with no held-defense outcome is not OD; a player who lost the position is MSR (`broken_defense`), not OD.
OD.annotation_guideline:
How to identify the sublabels for Successful Defense: Step 1 — Confirm the defense. Call `classify_opponent_interaction(start, end)`. Require `outcome: held_defense` with medium/high confidence. If the classifier does not return held defense with enough confidence, the section is not OD. Quote opponent-relative preflight phrases when available, such as driver started ahead of the opponent, driver ended ahead of the opponent, opponent drew alongside the driver, opponent was on the driver's left/right side, gap to the opponent shrank, driver gained relative speed, driver accelerated better than the opponent, and driver slowed more/less than the opponent. Step 2 — Pick the technique sub-label by how the opponent/player positions evolved, not solo-lap comparisons:
  - OD1 (inside cover at corner entry): opponent drew alongside the driver near the corner, but driver ended ahead of the opponent.
  - OD2 (defensive lift on a straight): gap to the opponent shrank on the straight, but the driver still ended ahead of the opponent.

EA.name: Expert Adherence (Training)
EA.description: Driver closely follows or cleanly outperforms the expert's line and speed profile. Look for **overall gap holds stable**, **gap shrinks**, player-ahead evidence, or a time gap below 200ms in the time delta when available, plus **speed match** or better speed with no instability. The player's **entry trajectory** and **exit trajectory** usually track the expert with trajectory offset **aligned** (within ±0.5 m of zero), but EA can still apply to a cleaner/faster line that is wider or tighter than the expert when there is no off-track/cutting/instability evidence and no MSP/RM/MSR/PS gate. A time gap below 200ms is not a mistake by itself; if the section is otherwise clean, categorize it as expert adherence.
EA.annotation_guideline: How to identify the sublabels for Expert Adherence (Training): The driver is following or cleanly outperforming the optimal racing line and speed profile closely. A time gap below 200ms is not a mistake by itself; when the rest of the evidence is clean, treat it as Expert Adherence. Nothing needs to be labeled right now.

PS.name: Pit Stop
PS.description: Driver is in the circuit's Pit section. Require pit evidence from position evidence that the segment overlaps the circuit's known Pit section. When Pit and the adjacent straight share the same normalized range, sustained pit-lane-style trajectory offset plus large player/expert speed separation or slow pit-exit acceleration can supply Pit-section procedure evidence. Do not label PS from dramatic speed reduction, trajectory deviation, or acceleration back toward track speed alone when the segment is away from the known Pit range.
PS.annotation_guideline: How to identify the sublabels for Pit Stop: Use PS for Pit-section procedure. First verify the segment position overlaps the Pit section, either directly or through a Pit-vs-adjacent-straight ambiguity supported by sustained pit-lane-style trajectory offset and large player/expert speed separation or slow pit-exit acceleration. Add PS1 only when the PS segment specifically shows pit-exit / rejoin behavior: accelerating out of Pit and merging back toward the racing line.

RM.name: Recovery & Merge
RM.description: Driver recovering from a prior mistake and merging back to the racing line. The trajectory offset shows **recovery** toward the expert line, with speed/throttle consistent with rejoining or accelerating back toward pace. Time delta may show **gap shrinks**, or may still show **gap grows** while `slope_shape` shows recovery shape. Do not infer RM from pit location alone.
RM.annotation_guideline: How to identify sublabels for Recovery & Merge: The driver is recovering from a mistake. Step 1: Analyze the 'Time Difference to Expert' graph with `compute_slope`; use its deterministic unit and trend-significance fields. A significant falling `total_change_direction` is strong RM evidence, but a significant rising total change can still be RM when `slope_shape` shows recovery shape and the action evidence shows recovery / merge rather than a new technical mistake. Tiny ms changes are not RM evidence. Step 2: Examine trajectory evidence to identify recovery - look for the driver line converging back toward the expert racing line from either side after a prior mistake/off-track, using near-line/toward-line verdict fields when available. Step 3: Examine the 'speed_delta' graph to identify if the player is accelerating back toward the expert's speed profile. Step 4: use the 'compute_expert_phases' tool (it produces a 'phase_indices' attachment contains the indices for entry/apex/exit). Do not infer RM from pit location alone.

MSP.name: Mistake (Practice)
MSP.description: Technical driving error causing time loss or vehicle instability, NOT caused by interaction with a close opponent. Time delta shows **gap grows** by at least 200ms and the trajectory offset shows a clear deviation from the expert's line (offset **wider than expert** or **tighter than expert**) that does not recover inside the range. A time gap below 200ms is not a mistake by itself; if the section is otherwise clean, use EA instead. If the dominant action is merge/rejoin recovery back toward the expert line, use RM instead even when the absolute time gap is still growing. When `classify_opponent_interaction` returns an adverse racing outcome (`failed_attack` or `broken_defense`), the section is MSR, not MSP.
MSP.annotation_guideline: How to identify sublabels for Practice Mistake: The driver has committed a technical driving error. Step 1: Analyze the 'Time Difference to Expert' graph with `compute_slope`; require `total_change_direction: "rising"`, `total_change_is_label_significant: true`, and at least 200ms of time-gap evidence for time-loss evidence, and cite `slope_shape` when the loss-rate slope changes over the section. Do not describe tiny positive ms changes as strong, and do not treat a time gap below 200ms as a mistake by itself. Do not use MSP when the trajectory is converging back toward the expert racing line and speed/throttle show a merge or rejoin recovery; that is RM even if the time gap still grows overall. Step 2: Examine the differences in 'throttle' between the player and the expert to identify when the driver applied too much or too little throttle, or got on/off the throttle at the wrong time. Step 3: Examine the differences in 'brake' between the player and the expert to identify if the driver braked too hard or too softly, or got on/off the brake at the wrong time. Step 4: Examine the 'trajectory_balance' graph to find understeer (blue / front-slip dominant) or oversteer (red / rear-slip dominant), which could lead to lower speed. Step 5: For entry/apex/exit shape questions, use trajectory evidence with the 'compute_expert_phases' tool on the same step (it produces a 'phase_indices' attachment contains the phase indices for entry/apex/exit). Step 6: Before committing in opponent-capable data, call `classify_opponent_interaction(start, end)` — if it returns `failed_attack` or `broken_defense`, the section is MSR, not MSP.

MSR.name: Mistake (Racing)
MSR.description: Time / position loss caused by an interaction with a close opponent. Required interaction evidence: `outcome: failed_attack` or `outcome: broken_defense` with medium/high confidence. Low / weak confidence requires opponent-trajectory inspection or omitting the label. If the evidence does not support an adverse racing outcome, this is not MSR.
MSR.annotation_guideline:
How to identify sublabels for Racing Mistake: Step 1 — Confirm the adverse racing outcome. Require `outcome: failed_attack` or `outcome: broken_defense` with medium/high confidence. If not, the section is not MSR. Step 2 — Pick the outcome family from opponent-relative facts:
  - Failed overtake attempt: opponent started ahead of the driver, the driver attacked or drew alongside the opponent, and the driver did not end ahead.
  - Defense broken: driver started ahead of the opponent, the opponent drew alongside the driver, and the gap flipped from driver ahead to opponent ahead.
Step 3 — Pick the specific subtype from opponent/player position and motion facts. Prefer a specific subtype over the generic label when the facts identify the attempt type:
  - MSR3 (failed O1 late-brake attack at entry): driver drew alongside the opponent under braking but did not end ahead.
  - MSR4 (failed O3 outside-line sweep): opponent was on the driver's inside side while the driver stayed outside, but the driver did not end ahead.
  - MSR5 (failed O4 switchback): opponent and driver swapped sides through the corner, but the gap did not flip to driver ahead.
  - MSR6 (failed O5 slipstream gain): gap to the opponent shrank on a straight and driver gained relative speed, but the gap did not flip to driver ahead.
  - MSR7 (broken OD1 inside cover): opponent drew alongside the driver near the corner and the gap flipped from driver ahead to opponent ahead.
  - MSR8 (broken OD2 defensive lift): gap to the opponent shrank on a straight and the gap flipped from driver ahead to opponent ahead.
  - MSR1 / MSR2: only when the attempt-type signature cannot be identified from the opponent-relative facts.

RM1.name: Recover from off-track
RM1.description: Driver returning to track after an off-track excursion — the trajectory offset peaks far **wider than expert** earlier in the segment (a prior **moving toward positive (widening)** beat), then shows **recovery** (offset trending back toward zero) while the speed trace shows the driver rejoining or accelerating back toward pace. Time delta may show **gap shrinks**, or a still-rising gap whose `slope_shape` shows recovery shape.

PS1.name: Exit pit lane
PS1.description: Driver re-joining the track from the Pit section - the segment position overlaps the circuit's known Pit section, and telemetry shows merge / recovery back toward the racing line. A Pit-vs-adjacent-straight ambiguity can count as Pit-section position when sustained pit-lane-style trajectory offset and large player/expert speed separation or slow pit-exit acceleration support pit procedure. This is pit procedure, not recovery from a mistake. Do not infer PS1 from low speed plus wide trajectory alone when the position is a normal racing section away from Pit.

RM5.name: Recover from speed gap over 20
RM5.description: Player more than 20 km/h slower than the expert with the speed gap closing — the speed delta shows **expert faster than player** with a **large gap section** (|Δ| > 20 km/h) that trends toward zero across the segment. Time delta may shrink, or may still grow while `slope_shape` shows recovery shape.

RM6.name: Recover from small speed gap under 20
RM6.description: Player less than 20 km/h slower than the expert with the speed gap closing — the speed delta shows **expert faster than player** without any **large gap section** (|Δ| stays ≤ 20 km/h). Time delta may shrink, or may still grow while `slope_shape` shows recovery shape.

RM7.name: Merge back to expert line
RM7.description: Player trajectory converging toward the expert line — the trajectory offset shows **recovery** (trending back toward zero from either side), typically across the **post-exit** span of a corner phase.

RM8.name: Accelerate earlier at exit
RM8.description: During recovery, the player's throttle **application onset is earlier than** the expert's around **at expert's exit (idx N, phase k)**, with a matching earlier **acceleration onset** on the speed trace. Time delta may shrink, or may still grow while `slope_shape` shows recovery shape.

RM9.name: Accelerate later at exit
RM9.description: During recovery, the player's throttle **application onset is later than** the expert's around **at expert's exit (idx N, phase k)**, with a matching later **acceleration onset** on the speed trace. Time delta may shrink, or may still grow while `slope_shape` shows recovery shape.

RM10.name: Brake earlier at entry
RM10.description: During recovery, the player's brake **initiation onset is earlier than** the expert's around **at expert's entry (idx N, phase k)**, with a matching earlier **deceleration onset** on the speed trace. Time delta may shrink, or may still grow while `slope_shape` shows recovery shape.

RM11.name: Brake later at entry
RM11.description: During recovery, the player's brake **initiation onset is later than** the expert's around **at expert's entry (idx N, phase k)**, with a matching later **deceleration onset** on the speed trace. Time delta may shrink, or may still grow while `slope_shape` shows recovery shape.

MSP1.name: Initiate brake too late
MSP1.description: The player's **brake initiation onset is later than** the expert's at corner entry, alongside the time **gap grows**. Player often **entry trajectory wider than expert** as they brake later.

MSP5.name: Initiate brake too early
MSP5.description: The player's **brake initiation onset is earlier than** the expert's at corner entry, alongside the time **gap grows**

MSP13.name: Highest brake pressure too low
MSP13.description: The player's **peak brake pressure is lower than** the expert. Player's entry trajectory wider than expert.

MSP22.name: Highest brake pressure too high
MSP22.description: The player's **peak brake pressure is higher than** the expert's across the braking phase, often leading to **speed gap growing** later,  **trajectory wider than expert ** later

MSP14.name: Brake applied too quickly
MSP14.description: The player's **brake initiation onset aligned with expert**, but **brake initiation end earlier than expert**. Player **apex trajectory wider than expert** often.

MSP24.name: Brake applied too slowly
MSP24.description: The player's **brake initiation onset aligned with expert**, but **brake initiation end later than expert**. Player **apex trajectory wider than expert** often.

MSP17.name: Release brake too quickly
MSP17.description: The player's **brake release onset aligned with expert**, but **brake release end earlier than expert**.  Player often **exit trajectory wider than expert** and **time gap grows** at exit.

MSP18.name: Release brake too slowly
MSP18.description: The player's **brake release onset aligned with expert**, but **brake release end later than expert**.  Player often **time gap grows** at exit.

MSP27.name: Initiate brake release too late
MSP27.description: The player's brake **release onset** later than the expert. causing **time gap grows** at exit.

MSP28.name: Initiate brake release too early
MSP28.description: The player's brake **release onset** earlier than the expert. causing **apex trajectory wider than expert** and **time gap grows** at exit.

MSP31.name: Highest brake length too short
MSP31.description: The player's interval between **brake initiation** end and **release onset** spans fewer indices than the expert's — **peak brake pressure** is held for a shorter span.

MSP32.name: Highest brake length too long
MSP32.description: The player's interval between **brake initiation** end and **release onset** spans more indices than the expert's — **peak brake pressure** is held for a longer span.

MSP34.name: Throttle and brake applied at the same time for too long
MSP34.description: The player **applies throttle and brake simultaneously** across a span where the expert shows no overlap.

MSP15.name: Throttle applied too quickly
MSP15.description: The player's **throttle application onset aligned with expert**, but **throttle application end earlier than expert**, often co-occurring with **oversteer** or **understeer**.

MSP25.name: Throttle applied too slowly
MSP25.description: The player's **throttle application onset aligned with expert**, but **throttle application end later than expert**, often co-occurring with **gap grows** in the time delta.

MSP20.name: Initiate throttle too early
MSP20.description: The player's throttle **application onset** earlier than the expert. understeer or oversteer occur which results in time loss and trajectory wider than expert

MSP21.name: Initiate throttle too late
MSP21.description: The player's throttle **application onset** later than the expert. no understeer or oversteer, which indicate poor utilization of grip which result in time loss

MSP23.name: Release throttle too quickly
MSP23.description: The player's throttle **release onset** aligned with expert, but player's throttle **release end** is earlier than the expert.  player's **brake initiation end** is earlier than the expert's. trajectory wider than expert at entry or apex

MSP29.name: Initiate throttle release too late
MSP29.description: The player's throttle **release onset** is later than the expert, and player's brake **initiation end** is later than the expert's. time gap rising at entry

MSP30.name: Initiate throttle release too early
MSP30.description: The player's throttle **release onset** is earlier than the expert's approaching corner entry, time gap rising at entry

MSP2.name: Initiate the turn too late
MSP2.description: The player **entry trajectory wider than expert** the expert's line. this causes **time gap rising at exit**

MSP6.name: Initiate the turn too early
MSP6.description: The player **entry trajectory tighter than expert** the expert. this causes **apex trajectory tighter than expert**, **time gap rising at exit** and **time gap rising at apex**

MSP3.name: Too late compared to expert Apex
MSP3.description: The player **reaches apex later than** the expert's apex index.

MSP7.name: Too early compared to expert Apex
MSP7.description: The player **reaches apex earlier than** the expert's apex index.

MSP4.name: Time to exit too early
MSP4.description: The player **apex trajectory aligned with expert**, but **exit trajectory wider than expert**

MSP8.name: Time to exit too late
MSP8.description: The player **apex trajectory aligned with expert**, but **exit trajectory wider than expert**

MSP9.name: Entry trajectory too tight
MSP9.description: The player's **entry trajectory tighter than expert** the expert. usually **brake initation onset eariler than expert**

MSP33.name: Entry trajectory too wide
MSP33.description: The player's **entry trajectory wider than expert**. usually **brake initiation onset later than expert** which causes understeer at the entry.

MSP10.name: Apex too wide
MSP10.description: The player's apex is **closer to outside** than the expert's at the expert's apex index, with offset **wider than expert**.

MSP11.name: Exit trajectory too narrow
MSP11.description: The player's **exit trajectory tighter than expert** the expert. **speed gap grow** at exit

MSP16.name: Exit trajectory too wide
MSP16.description: The player's **exit trajectory wider than expert** the expert.

MSP41.name: Cutting the line
MSP41.description: The player's trajectory **cuts inside** the expert's line across the corner (offset is **tighter than expert** at multiple phases).

MSP42.name: Inefficient grip utilization at entry
MSP42.description: Grip utilisation at corner entry deviates from the expert's pattern — an **over-limit spike**, **sustained over-limit** (**tire is sustained over its peak grip**), or **sustained low** appears across the index range where braking is active and speed is decreasing (the entry phase, cross-referenced with the trajectory or speed trace).

MSP43.name: Inefficient grip utilization at exit
MSP43.description: Grip utilisation at corner exit deviates from the expert's pattern — an **over-limit spike**, **sustained over-limit** (**tire is sustained over its peak grip**), or **sustained low** appears across the index range where throttle is being applied and speed is increasing (the exit phase, cross-referenced with the trajectory or speed trace).

MSP44.name: Oversteering at entry
MSP44.description: The player shows **oversteer** at the corner-entry phase.

MSP45.name: Understeering at entry
MSP45.description: The player shows **understeer** at the corner-entry phase.

MSP46.name: Oversteering at exit
MSP46.description: The player shows **oversteer** that at the corner-exit phase.

MSP47.name: Understeering at exit
MSP47.description: The player shows **understeer** at the corner-exit phase.

MSP35.name: Shift up too early
MSP35.description: Use when the player's **upshift** occurs at 2 or more index earlier than the expert's matching upshift.

MSP36.name: Shift up too late
MSP36.description: The player's **upshift** occurs at a 2 or more index later  than the expert's matching upshift.

MSP37.name: Shift down too early
MSP37.description: the player's **downshift** occurs at an 2 or more index earlier  than the expert's matching downshift at then entry

MSP38.name: Shift down too late
MSP38.description: the player's **downshift** occurs at an 2 or more index later  than the expert's matching downshift at then entry

MSP48.name: Gear too low when accelerating
MSP48.description: Use when the player is in a lower gear than the expert at the corner exit. The low/high verdict comes from comparing the player's exit gear with the expert's exit gear. Use this for the exit gear mismatch, not for the shift instant itself; if the main evidence is an upshift that happened late, prefer MSP36.

MSP49.name: Gear too high when accelerating
MSP49.description: Use when the player is in a higher gear than the expert at the corner exit. The low/high verdict comes from comparing the player's exit gear with the expert's exit gear. Use this for the exit gear mismatch, especially exit bogging, not for the shift instant itself; if the main evidence is a downshift that happened late, prefer MSP38.

MSR1.name: Failed overtake attempt (type unclear)
MSR1.description: Generic failed overtake attempt whose attempt-type signature cannot be read from the player's trace. Required interaction evidence: `outcome: failed_attack` with medium/high confidence. Prefer a specific subtype (MSR3 / MSR4 / MSR5 / MSR6) when the trace lets you identify which O-style attempt was tried; use MSR1 only when none of those match. Distinguished from O by the missing pass-completed outcome, and from MSP by the close opponent being the cause.

MSR2.name: Defense broken (type unclear)
MSR2.description: Generic broken defense whose defense-type signature cannot be read from the player's trace. Required interaction evidence: `outcome: broken_defense` with medium/high confidence. Prefer a specific subtype (MSR7 / MSR8) when the trace lets you identify which OD-style defense was tried; use MSR2 only when neither matches. Distinguished from OD by the broken-defense outcome instead of held defense.

MSR3.name: Failed late-brake attack at entry
MSR3.description: Failure-mirror of O1. Driver drew alongside the opponent under braking, often with the opponent on the driver's left/right side near corner entry, but the driver did not end ahead of the opponent. Required interaction outcome: `failed_attack` with medium/high confidence. Distinguished from O1 by the missing pass-completed outcome; distinguished from MSR1 by the identifiable under-braking alongside attempt.

MSR4.name: Failed outside-line sweep
MSR4.description: Failure-mirror of O3. Opponent was on the driver's inside side through the corner while the driver stayed outside, but the driver did not end ahead of the opponent. Required interaction outcome: `failed_attack` with medium/high confidence. Distinguished from O3 by the missing pass-completed outcome; from MSR1 by the identifiable outside-line opponent position; from MSP33 by the close opponent being the cause.

MSR5.name: Failed switchback
MSR5.description: Failure-mirror of O4. Opponent and driver swapped sides through the corner, or the side swap started, but the gap did not flip from opponent ahead to driver ahead by section end. Required interaction outcome: `failed_attack` with medium/high confidence. Distinguished from O4 by the missing pass-completed outcome; from MSR1 by the identifiable side-swap / cross-line signature.

MSR6.name: Failed slipstream gain on straight
MSR6.description: Failure-mirror of O5. On a straight section, gap to the opponent shrank and the driver gained relative speed, but the gap did not flip from opponent ahead to driver ahead. Required interaction outcome: `failed_attack` with medium/high confidence. Typically the straight ran out, the driver pulled out too late, or drew alongside the opponent too late for the pass to stick. Distinguished from O5 by the missing pass-completed outcome; from MSR1 by the identifiable straight-line closing signature.

MSR7.name: Inside cover broken (early-brake defense)
MSR7.description: Failure-mirror of OD1. Opponent drew alongside the driver near the corner and the gap flipped from driver ahead to opponent ahead. The opponent was often on the driver's left/right side while the driver tried to hold the inside. Required interaction outcome: `broken_defense` with medium/high confidence. Distinguished from OD1 by the broken-defense outcome; from MSR2 by the identifiable corner-defense position change.

MSR8.name: Defensive lift broken on straight
MSR8.description: Failure-mirror of OD2. On a straight, gap to the opponent shrank while the driver tried to hold position, and the gap flipped from driver ahead to opponent ahead. The driver may have slowed more than the opponent or accelerated worse after the lift. Required interaction outcome: `broken_defense` with medium/high confidence. Distinguished from OD2 by the broken-defense outcome; from MSR2 by the identifiable straight-line defense failure; from MSP25 by the close opponent being the cause.

O1.name: Late-brake attack at entry
O1.description: Driver drew alongside the opponent under braking near corner entry and the gap flipped from opponent ahead to driver ahead. Use this when the opponent started ahead of the driver, the driver drew alongside the opponent before or during the braking phase, and the driver ended ahead of the opponent.

O3.name: Outside-line sweep
O3.description: Opponent was on the driver's inside side through the corner while the driver stayed outside, and the driver ended ahead of the opponent. Use this when the outside position against the opponent is the reason the pass works, not when the driver merely runs wide without a close opponent.

O4.name: Switchback
O4.description: Opponent and driver swapped sides through the corner, then the gap flipped from opponent ahead to driver ahead on exit. Use this when the driver gives up one side early, crosses back to the other side, and exits ahead of the opponent.

O5.name: Slipstream gain on straight
O5.description: On a straight section, opponent started ahead of the driver, gap to the opponent shrank, driver gained relative speed, and the gap flipped from opponent ahead to driver ahead. Use this for straight-line draft / tow passes where the position change comes from opponent-relative speed.

OD1.name: Inside cover (early-brake defense)
OD1.description: Opponent drew alongside the driver near the corner, but the driver ended ahead of the opponent. Use this when the driver's position denied the opponent's corner attack; the label is decided from opponent/player position facts.

OD2.name: Defensive lift on straight
OD2.description: On a straight section, gap to the opponent shrank while the opponent attacked from behind, but the driver still ended ahead of the opponent. Use this when the driver holds position despite the opponent gaining relative speed or drawing alongside.

ST1.name: In the corner
ST1.description: Full segment covers entire corner — driver turning throughout (single curve, hairpin, continuous arc).

ST2.name: On the straight
ST2.description: Full segment on a straight section — minimal steering, full throttle, minimal curvature.

ST3.name: Approach to corner
ST3.description: Full segment only covering the braking zone before a corner: starts before the detected corner arc and ends before the apex.

ST4.name: Exit corner leading to straight
ST4.description: Segment covers the exit section of a corner that leads onto a straight — the car is still in the corner exit phase, with steering unwinding and throttle increasing. Do not use ST4 for a range that substantially includes the following straight after corner exit is complete.

ST5.name: Between consecutive corners
ST5.description: Short transition between two corners — brief connection, not a full straight.

ST6.name: Consecutive corners with no straight in between
ST6.description: Multiple corners with no intervening straight (S-shape, chicane, esses).

ST7.name: Constant-radius corner
ST7.description: Corner shape refinement: the corner keeps a consistent radius from entry through apex to exit, with smooth and steady curvature.

ST8.name: Increasing-radius corner
ST8.description: Corner shape refinement: the corner opens up after entry or apex; curvature decreases and radius increases toward exit.

ST9.name: Decreasing-radius corner
ST9.description: Corner shape refinement: the corner tightens from entry toward apex or exit; curvature increases and radius decreases.

ST10.name: Hairpin corner
ST10.description: Corner shape refinement: a near-180 U-turn identified by detected turn angle.

ST11.name: Chicane or esses
ST11.description: Corner shape refinement: linked left-right or right-left direction changes, including chicanes, esses, and S-bends.

ST12.name: Entry altitude uphill

category_guidelines.Segment Type: Use one base segment-shape label when clear: ST1 In the corner, ST2 On the straight, ST3 Approach to corner, ST4 Exit corner leading to straight, ST5 Between consecutive corners, or ST6 Consecutive corners with no straight in between. ST3 means the range starts before the detected corner arc and ends before the apex; do not use ST3 for a range that includes the apex or corner exit. ST4 means the exit section of the corner itself as it leads toward a straight; it does not mean a range that includes the completed corner plus a substantial portion of the following straight. For corner segments, optionally add one corner-shape refinement when clear: ST7 Constant-radius corner, ST8 Increasing-radius corner, ST9 Decreasing-radius corner, ST10 Hairpin corner, or ST11 Chicane or esses. Add a corner-shape refinement only when preflight corner-shape refinement reports the matching shape_key for the final range; non-empty phases alone are not enough. ST10 requires preflight corner-shape refinement to report the hairpin flag true: is_near_u_turn. Entry/apex/exit altitude labels (ST12-ST20) are phase-specific subsegment labels gated by preflight altitude trend and slope_angle_degrees for the matching phase; do not choose them from raw height difference alone. Do not attach them to a lap parent segment that covers the whole corner; use them only when the annotation range is the matching corner phase subsegment.
